agents.name: Grok Bot
agents.role: always-on bots, most of his tokens

surface_source.quote: This helps make the UI fast and responsive on desktop and mobile.

agents.quote: I started by using Bot for personal tasks instead of work things, but it quickly took over the majority of my tokens.

agents.name: Cursor

surface_source.quote: I would go back and forth with Cursor to build a plan, and then start the agent running in the cloud, mostly with Codex.

agents.quote: I'm very opinionated about products for engineers, and a heavy user of Cursor myself, so I often gathered customer feedback and made sure we were building the right thing.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.5
models.quote: The spend was about 70% Opus, 30% Codex due to their API pricing.

models.name: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max
models.quote: Throughout the project, I flipped between Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. Both performed very well, although I used them differently. For example, Codex performed better for long-running tasks, while Opus was significantly better at writing.

review_style.value: Reviews most of the code and tests it; Bugbot reviews every PR
review_style.quote: It’s worth noting that I did review most of the code and tested changes both manually and with automated tests. I also had Bugbot review all my PRs (example).

also.quote: I explicitly block any write/destructive actions and have it ask for my approval first.

harness.value: Always-running Grok Bots on their own cloud computer, connected to his X and Gmail
harness.quote: For example, I have bots that are connected to my X, Gmail, etc.

history.value: Cursor plan mode, then Cursor cloud agents
history.quote: A large portion of this project was built while I was away from my keyboard.

rules_files.value: AGENTS.md (pixo), added only after the model made mistakes
rules_files.quote: I started with zero custom rules. I only added a rules file later after the model got a few things wrong (e.g. used the wrong linting command, couldn’t remember how to generate the binary).

signature.caption: before every long agent run
signature.why: Our pick: he plans each change with the model in Cursor, then hands it to a cloud agent and walks away. That is how he built a whole Rust library without writing code by hand.
signature.quote: Plan mode in Cursor is one of the most underrated features.

archetype.why: He plans, then sends agents to the cloud, and now runs always-on bots that use most of his tokens.

signature_quote.value: The cost of abstractions with AI is very high.
signature_quote.more: Over-abstraction was always annoying and a code smell but now there’s an easy solution: spend tokens.
